content.title: About
content.content: Apple juice 100 % is a completely natural beverage made from selected apple varieties without added sugar, preservatives or flavorings. It has a bright aroma, a sweet‑tart taste and retains most of the vitamins and minerals found in fresh apples.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Apple juice is one of the most popular non‑alcoholic drinks worldwide.
Juice from different apple varieties varies in color, from light golden to deep amber.
"100 %" guarantees that no extra sugar or water has been added.
Apple juice is often used in cooking for marinades, sauces and desserts.
In some countries it is a traditional drink for autumn festivals.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in apple juice help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Pectin, a soluble fiber, promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: May reduce cardiovascular risk
items.content: Regular consumption of apple juice can help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Hydrating
items.content: The drink is almost entirely water, aiding overall hydration.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Even without added sugar, natural fruit sugars can be significant; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature may irritate sensitive teeth and stomachs.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to apple juice.

items.title: Pasteurization
items.content: To extend shelf life, juice is often pasteurized, which can slightly reduce some vitamin levels.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Apple juice can be enjoyed chilled as a refreshing drink, used in smoothies, cocktails, sauces, or as a base for marinades. It pairs well with cinnamon, ginger and honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: After opening, keep the juice refrigerated in a tightly sealed bottle and consume within 5‑7 days. Unopened bottles should be stored in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight.

content.title: About
content.content: Ginger ale is a non‑alcoholic beverage made by carbonating water flavored with ginger extract and sweetener. It has a mild sweetness, a refreshing ginger taste, and characteristic fizz.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first ginger ale was created in England in the 19th century as a tonic.
There are two main styles: “dry” and “soft,” differing in the intensity of ginger flavor.
Ginger ale is a common mixer in cocktails such as the Moscow Mule.
In some cultures it is considered a traditional home remedy for colds.

items.title: Soothes the stomach
items.content: Ginger has anti‑inflammatory properties and can help relieve nausea and indigestion.

items.title: Provides hydration
items.content: Like any carbonated drink, it contributes to fluid intake, especially in warm weather.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Ginger extract is rich in gingerol, a compound with antioxidant activity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Most commercial ginger ales contain high amounts of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and tooth decay.

items.title: Carbonation
items.content: Excessive consumption of carbonated drinks may cause bloating and discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Ginger allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to ginger.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ginger ale chilled, use it as a cocktail mixer, add to marinades, or incorporate into batters for a subtle spice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days.
